From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Targeted region outage — routing guidance and recovery checklist

Hi Sara / Contoso Ops team,

Quick note to confirm what you may have seen in the observability alerts: between 08:03–08:54 PST this morning a cloud provider routing issue caused elevated error rates and timeouts for requests routed to two availability zones in our US-west region. That impacted a subset of customers using our hosted API where the smart-router had pinned traffic to those AZs.

Immediate customer-facing actions we recommend (applies to Acme Apps and other affected customers):
- Switch your Redwood endpoint region to us-west-2-failover or to eu-central-1 if low-latency EU routing is preferred. (See quick steps in attachment: reroute-playbook-v2.pdf)
- If you use pinned model variants, revert to the fallback model group (alias: rdx-multi-compat) while we validate KV caches.
- Increase client retry timeout to 10s for the next 6 hours and enable exponential backoff.

Internal notes: Marissa is coordinating capacity and automated reroute policies. Hannah will prepare a short timeline and include the audit artifacts you requested. Jonas will own the account communications follow-up.

I'll keep this thread open for updates. Please confirm when you've switched your endpoint or if you want Redwood to flip routing on your behalf (we can do that for customers with dedicated subscriptions).

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute-playbook-v2.pdf (3 pages, checklist), incident-timeline-20261205.csv

Subject: Post-incident timeline and temporary mitigation summary (draft)

Hi all,

Draft timeline attached and summary below; attaching postmortem summary and the incident timeline CSV. Please review — I'll finalize Monday and attach the SOC/audit snippets requested by Acme.

Summary (concise):
- 08:03 PST — Provider routing mesh reported increased control-plane reconciliation; Redwood router began queuing where AZ-specific endpoints failed health checks
- 08:05–08:32 PST — Elevated 5xx observed for ~12% of requests for customers pinned to us-west-A/B endpoints
- 08:55 PST — Marissa executed staged routing policy to shift traffic for affected accounts (A-9931, C-4402) to eu-central-1 and us-east-1 fallback pools; synthetic validation green at +3m
- 09:10 PST — Metrics normalized, residual latency spike through 09:45 while KV caches warmed

Customer-facing mitigation steps taken:
- Performed targeted policy flips for affected accounts (on behalf of customers who requested it)
- Provided playbook to customers for self-retry/reroute settings
- Generated incident timeline and shared initial artifacts

Open items:
- Root cause analysis (provider-side routing mesh configuration) — vendor engagement in progress
- Request from Acme for audit artifacts (logs, signed timeline) — Hannah to supply by EOD Mon
- Confirm whether to publish Customer Advisory (we recommend a short advisory for all customers in the US region)

Attachments: postmortem-summary-20261207.docx, incident-timeline-20261205.csv

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Folks — final update and next steps. Thank you for your patience.

What we delivered:
- Signed timeline and incident CSV (attached: postmortem-summary-20261207.docx, incident-timeline-20261205.csv)
- Temporary reroute executed for affected customers; synthetic validations and token-level metrics are included in the CSV
- List of accounts we proactively flipped: A-9931 (Acme Apps), C-4402 (Contoso), P-2100 (Nearshore Partners)

Dedicated instances note: no dedicated (customer-managed) on-prem instances were impacted; the incident affected Redwood-hosted routing tied to provider control-plane behavior. We'll provide a short advisory clarifying this for procurement.

Next steps and offers:
- Hannah to finalize RCA with provider engagement (ETA: 48 hrs) and provide the SOC/audit snippets requested by Contoso and Acme
- We'll publish a brief Customer Advisory to all customers in US region tomorrow morning unless you object
- Offer: Redwood will run a one-hour simulated failover test for your integration teams (we can schedule during your maintenance window). Please reply with preferred times.

If you want Redwood to perform any further policy flips or a scheduled simulated failover, reply to this thread and mark which accounts.

Thanks again,
Evelyn Hart
